description: A diaphone's blast: a buzzing tone of strong harmonics, the piston's note, through a low-pass that opens as the blast swells, a horn's tone brightening as it grows louder (Risset and Mathews 1969); its pitch sags from pitch to sag as the air runs out ('210 Hz falling to 170 Hz', Gamewell's measured diaphones), and it ends in the grunt, a suddenly lowered pitch, grunt times the last, over its last gruntTime (IHO S-12; the grunt 93–150 Hz, Laser 2007). harmonics are the partials' levels. A point source: its level falls 6 dB each time the distance doubles from near metres. Frequencies in Hz, times in seconds, levels as gains.
